title: Who ends with more marbles, {{NAME_3}} or {{NAME_2}}?
description: Two sums are compared without working out either total, by imagining two children who each get more marbles. Keeko doubts the answer and thinks the first sum must be greater because it starts higher.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two sums by how much each number changes, not by their totals. Watch for children who pick the sum that starts with the bigger number.

video_script.why: The child compares two sums by thinking about how much each number differs.
video_script.substitution: Imagine two children who each get more marbles, and compare the start and the gain.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_3}} and {{NAME_2}} with their marbles, before and after today
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the sum that starts with the bigger number and ignores that {{NAME_2}} gets three more marbles today.
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_2}} ends with two more marbles than {{NAME_3}}

final_answer.spoken: one thousand twenty three plus one hundred twenty five is less than one thousand twenty two plus one hundred twenty eight, and the second is greater by two

names.{{NAME_3}}: the child who had 1023 marbles and got 125 more
names.{{NAME_2}}: the child who had 1022 marbles and got 128 more

video_script.design: One idea: compare sums by the changes in the numbers. Assumes taking away to find a difference. Wrong idea: the sum that starts higher is greater. The two children and their marbles stay all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two sums side by side: 1023 + 125 and 1022 + 128

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.ask: a question mark glows between the two sums

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first sum is one thousand twenty three plus one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second sum is one thousand twenty two plus one hundred twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is greater, without working out either total?

beats.on_screen: the two sums stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two rows of marbles: {{NAME_3}} with 1023 and a lot more arriving, {{NAME_2}} with 1022 and a little more arriving

marks.kabir: {{NAME_3}} appears with a row of 1023 marbles and 125 more arriving
marks.name2: {{NAME_2}} appears with a row of 1022 marbles and 128 more arriving

narration: <bookmark mark='kabir'/>Imagine {{NAME_3}} had one thousand twenty three marbles and got one hundred twenty five more today.
<bookmark mark='name2'/>{{NAME_2}} had one thousand twenty two marbles and got one hundred twenty eight more.

marks.given: the two sums are written with the two names

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one sum for {{NAME_3}} and one sum for {{NAME_2}}.

beats.on_screen: To find: who ends with more marbles

marks.find: the words who ends with more marbles are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find who ends with more marbles, without working out either total.

marks.start: the two starting numbers are compared and the difference 1 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step one, compare the start. {{NAME_3}} has one thousand twenty three and {{NAME_2}} has one thousand twenty two. {{NAME_3}} starts with one more.

marks.gain: the two gains 125 and 128 are compared

narration: <bookmark mark='gain'/>Step two, compare what each gets today. {{NAME_2}} gets one hundred twenty eight and {{NAME_3}} gets one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>One hundred twenty eight minus one hundred twenty five is three, so {{NAME_2}} gets three more.

marks.net: the gain 3 and the start 1 are set against each other and the result 2 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='net'/>Step three, put the two together. {{NAME_2}} gets three more but starts with one less, so three minus one leaves two more.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_2}} ends with two more marbles than {{NAME_3}}. The second sum is the greater one.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows: the first sum is greater, because it starts with 1023; beside it, {{NAME_2}} gets 3 more and starts only 1 behind; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the extra 3 and the extra 1 appear and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the first sum is greater, because it starts with the bigger number.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But {{NAME_2}} gets three more today and starts only one behind. The extra three is more than the extra one.
